description: Erection of 20 two storey dwellings (Class C3) with accommodation in the roof with associated access, landscaping, parking and cycle storage and communal refuse storage.
decision_conditions: Occupier
The development must be begun not later than the expiration of three years beginning with the date hereof.Reason: To comply with Section 91 of the Town and Country Planning Act 1990, as amended.

Prior to the commencement of any above-ground construction works, a technical scheme of acoustic insulation for the dwellings (including glazing and acoustic ventilation) shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. The scheme shall ensure internal noise standards comply with BS8233:2014.Reason: To protect future occupiers from external noise and ensure a high standard of residential amenity, in accordance with Policies 29 and 33 of the Sutton Local Plan 2018 and Policy D14 of the London Plan 2021.

No dwelling hereby approved shall be occupied until any remediation works approved as per the Contaminated Land Assessment and associated Remediation Strategy (approved as a separate condition) have been completed, and a Verification/Closure Report confirming compliance has been submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority.Reason: To ensure the land has been made safe for residential occupation, in accordance with Policy 34 of the Sutton Local Plan 2018.

No building hereby permitted shall be occupied until evidence (photographs and installation contracts) is submitted to demonstrate that the sustainable drainage scheme has been completed in accordance with the approved strategy, alongside an updated Management and Maintenance Plan confirming routine maintenance tasks for all components for the lifetime of the development.Reason: To ensure the drainage scheme is fully operational and maintained, in accordance with Policy 32 of the Sutton Local Plan 2018 and Policy SI 13 of the London Plan 2021.

Prior to first occupation, 'as-built' Standard Assessment Procedure (SAP) outputs and documentary evidence shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority to demonstrate that the dwellings have achieved the targeted reductions in CO2 emissions through the installed Air Source Heat Pumps and Solar PVs. Operational performance shall thereafter be reported in line with GLA 'Be Seen' guidance.Reason: To verify the delivery of energy efficiency targets, in accordance with Policy 31 of the Sutton Local Plan 2018 and Policy SI 2 of the London Plan 2021.

Prior to first occupation, a completed Water Efficiency Calculator for New Dwellings shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority, demonstrating that internal potable water consumption for each dwelling will not exceed 105 litres per person per day (plus 5 litres for external use).Reason: To ensure sustainable water resource management, in accordance with Policy 31 of the Sutton Local Plan 2018 and Policy SI 5 of the London Plan 2021.

Prior to first occupation, documentary evidence confirming that the cooling and overheating mitigation measures have been implemented in accordance with the approved CIBSE TM59 Analysis shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority.Reason: To protect future occupiers from overheating risk, in accordance with Policy 33 of the Sutton Local Plan 2018 and Policy SI 4 of the London Plan 2021.

No dwelling hereby approved shall be occupied until the on-site car parking spaces (including electric vehicle charging infrastructure), secure and covered cycle storage, and communal/private refuse and recycling stores have been fully constructed, laid out, and made available for use in accordance with the approved drawings. These facilities shall thereafter be permanently retained.Reason: To ensure adequate parking, active travel, and waste facilities are provided on-site, in accordance with Policies 36 and 37 of the Sutton Local Plan 2018, and Policies T5, T6, and T6.1 of the London Plan 2021.

Prior to first occupation, a Statement of Conformity signed by a qualified ecologist (confirming completion of habitat creation and wildlife features) and an Information Pack for Residents highlighting site wildlife features and biodiversity gardening actions shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority.Reason: To verify the delivery of ecological enhancements, in accordance with Policy 26 of the Sutton Local Plan 2018.

The rating level of noise emitted from any fixed plant or machinery installed on site (including Air Source Heat Pumps) shall operate at least 5 dB(A) below the existing background noise level (LA90) as measured 1 metre from the window of any room of a neighbouring residential property.Reason: To safeguard residential acoustic amenity, in accordance with Policies 29 and 33 of the Sutton Local Plan 2018 and Policy D14 of the London Plan 2021

No development (excluding site clearance and demolition) shall commence until a final Biodiversity Gain Plan (BGP) and a 30-year Habitat Management and Monitoring Plan (HMMP) have been submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority.The submitted documents shall include:The completed Statutory Biodiversity Metric demonstrating the final baseline and post-development unit calculations;Details of on-site habitat creation, enhancement, and post-development management regimes;Confirmation of any required off-site biodiversity unit allocation/purchase (if an on-site shortfall remains);A 30-year management schedule detailing ecological maintenance tasks and monitoring report submission dates (in years 1, 3, 5, 7, 10, 15, 20, 25, and 30 post-completion).The development shall thereafter be carried out, managed, and monitored strictly in accordance with the approved BGP and HMMP for a minimum of 30 years post-completion.Reason: To ensure the mandatory delivery, long-term management, and monitoring of Biodiversity Net Gain in accordance with Policy 26 of the Sutton Local Plan 2018, Policy G6 of the London Plan 2021, and Schedule 7A of the Town and Country Planning Act 1990.

No development (including demolition, site preparation, and groundworks) shall commence until a detailed Construction Environmental Management Plan (CEMP) has been submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. The CEMP shall include, but not be limited to:Site working hours (restricted to 08:00-18:00 Mondays to Fridays, 08:00-13:00 on Saturdays, and none on Sundays or Bank Holidays);Construction vehicle routing, delivery management, and loading/unloading arrangements;Dust control and suppression measures;Emission standards for Non-Road Mobile Machinery (NRMM) in compliance with GLA requirements;Noise and vibration mitigation measures in accordance with BS5228;Waste management, site security fencing, and wheel-washing facilities;An Ecological Clerk of Works (ECoW) schedule, precautionary species method statements (including removal of tree T25), and mammal protection measures.The development shall thereafter be implemented strictly in accordance with the approved CEMP.Reason: To protect local residential amenity, highway safety, air quality, and biodiversity during construction, in accordance with Policies 26, 29, 34, and 36 of the Sutton Local Plan 2018, and Policies D14, G6, SI 1, and T4 of the London Plan 2021.

No development (including demolition, site preparation, or groundworks) shall commence until a comprehensive Arboricultural Method Statement (AMS) and Tree Protection Plan (TPP) in accordance with BS5837:2012 have been submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. The details shall specify protective fencing and ground protection measures around all retained trees (including T1 Sequoia, T24 Horse Chestnut, and T28 London Plane). The approved tree protection measures shall be erected prior to any site works and maintained throughout construction.Reason: To safeguard mature feature trees that make a vital contribution to the character and visual amenity of the area, in accordance with Policy 28 of the Sutton Local Plan 2018 and Policy G7 of the London Plan 2021.

No development (other than site clearance and investigation works) shall commence until a Contaminated Land Assessment and associated Remediation Strategy based on a Phase 2 intrusive investigation (focusing on concerns in Phase 1 Report ref. J25-041-R01) has been submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority.Reason: To ensure that risks from land contamination to future users of the land and neighbouring land are minimised, in accordance with Policy 34 of the Sutton Local Plan 2018 and Policy SD1 of the London Plan 2021.

No development shall commence until detailed engineering, crossover, and construction drawings for the highway modification works on Denmark Road and Langcroft Close have been submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority in consultation with the Highway Authority.Reason: To ensure safe and suitable vehicular and pedestrian access is provided on the public highway, in accordance with Policies 36 and 37 of the Sutton Local Plan 2018 and Policy T4 of the London Plan 2021.

No development (excluding site investigations and demolition) shall commence until a revised, detailed Sustainable Drainage Strategy for the site—which maximises infiltration and multifunctionality based on full site-specific BRE365 testing—has been submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority in consultation with the Lead Local Flood Authority. The submission shall include detailed drainage drawings, hydraulic calculations, and structural specifications for all surface water components.Reason: To ensure surface water is managed safely and sustainably in accordance with the drainage hierarchy, preventing flood risk on and off-site, pursuant to Policy 32 of the Sutton Local Plan 2018 and Policy SI 13 of the London Plan 2021.

Prior to the commencement of any above-ground construction works, samples and product specifications for all external facing materials—including brickwork, roofing, dormer cladding, windows, doors, and boundary treatments—shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. The development shall be constructed strictly in accordance with the approved details.Reason: To ensure a high-quality external appearance that respects local character and preserves the setting of the adjacent Wrythe Green Conservation Area, in accordance with Policies 28 and 30 of the Sutton Local Plan 2018 and Policy D3 of the London Plan 2021.

Prior to the commencement of any above-ground construction works, a detailed Hard and Soft Landscaping Scheme shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. The scheme shall include:Planting plans specifying the planting of 43 new deciduous trees (including species, sizes, and numbers);Hard surfacing materials, including permeable paving and grasscrete details;Boundary treatments, including walls, fencing, and hedgehog holes;Detailed design, safety surfacing, and equipment for the central play area under tree T28;Proposals for the repurposing of timber from the T25 Mulberry tree and the erection of an informative historic plaque.All landscaping works shall be implemented in accordance with the approved scheme.Reason: To ensure high-quality public realm, visual amenity, and ecological connectivity, in accordance with Policies 26 and 28 of the Sutton Local Plan 2018 and Policies D3, G5, and G7 of the London Plan 2021.

Prior to rising above damp proof course level, a scheme for integrated wildlife and nesting features shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. The scheme shall include at a minimum:1no. integrated multi-chamber swift brick per dwelling;1no. integrated house sparrow terrace per dwelling;1no. integrated bat roost per dwelling;1no. integrated solitary bee brick per dwelling.The approved features shall be installed prior to first occupation and retained thereafter.Reason: To enhance the biodiversity value of the site, in accordance with Policy 26 of the Sutton Local Plan 2018 and Policy G6 of the London Plan 2021.

Prior to above-ground construction works, full specifications, layout plans, and orientation drawings for the roof-mounted Solar Photovoltaic (PV) system shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority.Reason: To ensure on-site renewable energy generation is maximised, in accordance with Policy 31 of the Sutton Local Plan 2018 and Policy SI 2 of the London Plan 2021.

Notwithstanding the provisions of the Town and Country Planning (General Permitted Development) (England) Order 2015 (or any Order revoking and re-enacting that Order), no extensions, roof alterations/dormers, or outbuildings falling within Classes A, B, C, D, or E of Part 1 of Schedule 2 shall be erected on any dwelling or within their curtilages without express planning permission.Reason: To prevent overdevelopment, safeguard private amenity space, protect RPAs of retained trees, and preserve the visual character of the street scene and adjacent Wrythe Green Conservation Area, in accordance with Policies 28, 29, and 30 of the Sutton Local Plan 2018.

The development must be carried out in accordance with the provisions of the Fire Statement by Mu.Studio Revision 01 dated 09.07.2025.Reason: To ensure that the development incorporates the necessary fire safety measures in accordance with the Mayor's London Plan Policy D12.
